## The login branch

Your login response carries a `token_type` that is *not always* `"Bearer"`. Branch on it
before treating the response as a session:

```ts
import { isSetupRequired, isVerificationRequired, type LoginResult } from "@/services/auth/two-factor/types";

const result: LoginResult = await login(credentials);

if (isSetupRequired(result)) {
  // no 2FA configured yet - navigate to the setup screen, carrying result.accessToken
} else if (isVerificationRequired(result)) {
  // 2FA already configured - navigate to the OTP challenge, carrying result.accessToken
} else {
  // result.tokenType === "Bearer" - a normal session, no 2FA involved
}
```

`result.accessToken` in the two 2FA branches is **not a session token** - it's a
short-lived, encrypted challenge token. Hold it in memory only (a store that is not
persisted to `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`), and resend it as the `token` argument
to every `two-factor/api.ts` function below until the flow completes.

## API contract

| Function | Path | Auth | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `setupTwoFactor` | `2fa/setup` | challenge token | Returns the QR SVG, the manual-entry secret, and the recovery codes - show all three once |
| `completeTwoFactor` | `2fa/complete` | challenge token | Same OTP screen serves setup-confirm and login-verify - see "Screens shipped" below |
| `verifyRecoveryCode` | `2fa/verify-recovery-code` | challenge token | Lost-device path; returns `remainingRecoveryCodes` so the UI can warn near zero |
| `requestTwoFactorReset` | `2fa/request-reset` | real access token | Re-validates the password before issuing a reset challenge token |
| `resetTwoFactor` | `2fa/reset` | reset challenge token | Clears the secret; the user re-enrolls through setup afterward |
| `disableTwoFactor` | `2fa/disable` | real access token | Fails with 403 when `google2fa.mandatory` is `true` on the backend - surface that error, don't hide the button |
| `regenerateRecoveryCodes` | `2fa/regenerate-recovery-codes` | real access token | Screen shipped - see "Account management" below |

Two of these paths are a deliberate departure from the IDR reference this package's
backend contract otherwise matches almost exactly: IDR groups its equivalents under
`/auth/verify-recovery-code` and `/auth/regenerate-recovery-codes`. This package
groups every 2FA operation under `/2fa/*` instead, per `docs/google-2fa.md`, and the
routes stub this installer wired for you follows that grouping - so the paths above
are the ones that are actually live once `two-factor-auth.php` is required.

## Screens shipped

**Ported from IDR** (`idr-front`'s `/2fa*` routes are a working reference for these):

- **Setup / QR** - render the `qr` SVG returned by `setupTwoFactor` (sanitize before
  `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` if you go that route), show the manual-entry `secret`,
  and hold onto `recoveryCodes` for the display screen below.
- **OTP challenge** - a single 6-digit-code screen, dual-purpose: reached either right
  after setup (to confirm enrollment) or on every subsequent login once 2FA is
  configured. Both cases call `completeTwoFactor` with the same challenge token.
- **Recovery codes display** - show `recoveryCodes` once, right after setup; IDR
  doesn't persist or offer a download for these, only copy-to-clipboard.
- **Recovery-code challenge** - the "lost my device" path off the OTP challenge
  screen, calling `verifyRecoveryCode` instead of `completeTwoFactor`.

**Account management - designed fresh, no IDR screen exists for these, shipped as
`src/routes/_private/security/-components/two-factor-section.tsx` and the three
dialogs it composes:**

- **Disable 2FA (self-service)** - IDR only ships an *admin* reset dialog against a
  different, admin-scoped endpoint; it has no end-user "turn off my own 2FA" screen.
  `disable-two-factor-dialog.tsx` is a password-confirmation form calling
  `disableTwoFactor`, surfacing the 403 `mandatory` case above instead of assuming
  the action always succeeds.
- **Reset flow** - also absent from IDR. `request-two-factor-reset-dialog.tsx`
  (password confirm, while still holding a real access token) hands its resulting
  challenge token to `src/routes/(public)/_guest/two-factor/reset/page.tsx`
  (`resetTwoFactor`) through the URL, the same way the setup/login challenge tokens
  travel between screens - the two ship together because the reset link goes nowhere
  without the guest-side confirm page.
- **Regenerate recovery codes** - `regenerate-recovery-codes-dialog.tsx`, same
  password-confirmation shape, reusing the recovery-codes display component from the
  setup flow to show the new set.
